source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which liver enzyme is most specific to liver cell damage?
questions.rationale: ALT (SGPT) is produced mainly by the liver, making it the most specific liver enzyme.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Serum enzymes (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: ALT is thc most specific indicator of liver function because it is produced only by the liver.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During liver biopsy needle insertion, the client is told to:
questions.rationale: Exhaling and holding the breath keeps the diaphragm still and prevents injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Liver biopsy (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: Instruct client to exhale deeply; hold breath for 5-10 seconds, during needle insertion.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After liver biopsy, the client is positioned on the right side to:
questions.rationale: Lying on the right side presses on the puncture site; bleeding is the most common complication.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Liver biopsy (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: Turn the client to right side for 4 hours to apply pressure and prevent bleeding.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before paracentesis, the nurse asks the client to:
questions.rationale: Emptying the bladder prevents accidental bladder puncture; the client sits upright.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Paracentesis (PDF p. 218)
questions.quote: Ask client to empty the bladder to prevent puncture.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a large-volume paracentesis, the nurse watches especially for:
questions.rationale: Removing protein-rich ascitic fluid can shift fluid and cause hypovolemia and shock.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Paracentesis (PDF p. 218)
questions.quote: Signs and symptoms of hypovolemic shock.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The primary pathophysiology underlying the complications of liver cirrhosis is:
questions.rationale: Fibrosis obstructs flow and raises portal pressure, causing varices, ascites and splenomegaly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Liver cirrhosis (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: These 3 factors eventually lead to portal hypertension (the primary pathophysiology of liver cirrhosis).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is often the earliest sign of liver cirrhosis?
questions.rationale: Anorexia is an early sign of impaired liver function; ascites, jaundice and asterixis come later.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Liver cirrhosis (PDF p. 220)
questions.quote: Anorexia is an initial manifestation to liver function impairment.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ascites in cirrhosis results from portal hypertension and:
questions.rationale: Low albumin lowers colloid osmotic pressure, shifting fluid into the peritoneal cavity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Ascites (PDF p. 221)
questions.quote: Ascites is also due to hypoalbuminemia.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with cirrhosis has a flapping tremor of the hands when the wrists are extended. This is:
questions.rationale: Asterixis (liver flap) reflects elevated ammonia and impending hepatic encephalopathy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Asterixis (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: This results from neurologic function impairment due to elevated serum ammonia levels.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diuretic is the drug of choice for ascites in cirrhosis?
questions.rationale: Spironolactone counters the high aldosterone of cirrhosis; furosemide may be added.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Relieve ascites (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: Ihe drug of choice is Aldactone (Spironolactone)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: To monitor ascites, the nurse measures daily:
questions.rationale: Daily weights, abdominal girth and intake and output track fluid accumulation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Relieve ascites (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: Monitor daily weights, abdominal girth; intake and output

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with esophageal varices should be taught to avoid:
questions.rationale: Straining, shouting, coughing, lifting and rough or spicy foods raise pressure and can rupture varices.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Prevent rupture of varices (PDF p. 224)
questions.quote: Straining at stool (administer stool softeners as prescribed).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on lactulose for high ammonia has 3 soft stools a day. The nurse recognizes this as:
questions.rationale: Lactulose acidifies the colon and traps ammonia; 2–3 soft stools daily is expected. Report more than 4.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Reduce ammonia (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: If it is mote than 4 watery stools a day, notify the physician.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The most important teaching for a client with alcoholic cirrhosis is to:
questions.rationale: Avoiding alcohol is the most important teaching; avoid aspirin (bleeding) and high sodium.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Cirrhosis management (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: Most important client teaching: Avoid alcohol.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Several children in a barangay with a contaminated water source develop jaundice. If this is hepatitis A, the most likely mode of transmission is:
questions.rationale: HAV spreads fecal-orally via contaminated water, food, shellfish and poor sanitation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Hepatitis A (PDF p. 226)
questions.quote: Transmission: feco o— oral route, contaminated water or milk, uncooked shellfish

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis virus can only infect a person who also has hepatitis B?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis D (delta agent) requires co-infection with hepatitis B.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Hepatitis D (PDF p. 227)
questions.quote: Co —infection of hepatitis B.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis is waterborne and linked to poor sewage disposal?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis E spreads like hepatitis A, via contaminated water where sanitation is poor.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Hepatitis E (PDF p. 227)
questions.quote: Is waterborne virus. Prevalent in areas where sewage disposal is inadequate

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which home teaching is correct for a client with hepatitis A?
options: Do not prepare food for the family
questions.rationale: Strict handwashing, no food preparation for others, separate utensils and towels, no alcohol, no blood donation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Client education for hepatitis (PDF p. 227)
questions.quote: The client must not prepare food for other family members.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A woman has RUQ pain radiating to the right shoulder blade after a fatty meal. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Gallbladder pain follows fatty meals, radiates to the right scapula and comes with fat intolerance and belching.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Cholelithiasis (PDF p. 229)
questions.quote: Epigastric pain that radiates to the scapula 2 to 4 hours after eating fatty foods

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A gallstone blocks the common bile duct. Stools will likely be:
questions.rationale: Without bile pigment reaching the bowel, stools become acholic (pale, gray, clay-colored).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Biliary obstruction (PDF p. 229)
questions.quote: Acholic stool (pale/gray/clay — colored stool)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with biliary obstruction is at risk for bleeding because of poor absorption of:
questions.rationale: Absent bile prevents vitamin K absorption, lowering clotting factors; vitamin K may be given before surgery.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Biliary obstruction (PDF p. 229)
questions.quote: Decreased vitamin K absorption in the colon (leads to bleeding tendencies).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After laparoscopic cholecystectomy, a client reports shoulder pain. The nurse explains it is due to:
questions.rationale: Abdominal insufflation with CO2 irritates the diaphragm, causing referred shoulder pain and bloating.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (PDF p. 231)
questions.quote: the client normally experiences bloatedness and abdominal pain 'that radiates to the shoulders

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After choledochotomy, the T-tube drainage bag should be kept:
questions.rationale: Keeping the bag below the gallbladder allows excess bile to drain by gravity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 T-tube (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: The drainage bottle should be placed in bed, below the level of the gallbladder.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The main purpose of a T-tube after common bile duct exploration is to:
options: Drain bile while the duct heals
questions.rationale: It drains bile, keeps the swollen duct patent and prevents bile peritonitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 T-tube (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: To drain bile from the common bile duct and minimize amount of bile flowing into the duodenum.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lab is the most specific indicator of acute pancreatitis?
questions.rationale: Lipase is solely pancreatic in origin; amylase is also elevated.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: Elevated serum lipase (one of the most specific indicators of acute pancreatitis because lipase is solely of pancreatic origin).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bluish discoloration around the umbilicus in severe pancreatitis is:
questions.rationale: Cullen's sign is periumbilical; Grey Turner's is on the flanks; both signal hemorrhagic pancreatitis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: Cullen's sign (periumbilical area)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with acute pancreatitis has muscle twitching. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Calcium deposits in areas of fat necrosis, causing hypocalcemia (twitching, tetany).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: Hypocalcemia. Calcium is deposited in areas of fatty necrosis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which position may ease the pain of acute pancreatitis?
questions.rationale: Sitting up with knees flexed and a pillow against the abdomen relieves pain; supine worsens it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis management (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: sitting in bed with the knees flexed and pressing a pillow over the abdomen

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During acute pancreatitis, the client is kept NPO because food:
questions.rationale: Food stimulates pancreatic enzymes and worsens inflammation; an NGT may decompress the stomach.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis management (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: Food ingestion increases pancreatic secretion, which may increase inflammation and pain.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should pancreatic enzyme replacements be taken?
questions.rationale: Enzymes must be taken with food to digest it; absence of steatorrhea shows effectiveness.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis management (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: These medications should be taken with each meal and snack.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does a client know pancreatic enzyme therapy is working?
questions.rationale: Resolution of steatorrhea indicates adequate fat digestion.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Pancreatitis management (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: Absence of steatorrhea indicates effectiveness of the medications.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The Whipple procedure for pancreatic cancer removes the head of the pancreas, the duodenum, part of the stomach and the:
questions.rationale: Whipple removes the pancreatic head, distal stomach, duodenum and common bile duct, with reconstruction.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 8 Cancer of the pancreas (PDF p. 235)
questions.quote: Common bile duct (CBD)
